articles.title: Aces' Jewell Loyd downgraded to out for Wednesday's playoff game vs. Valkyries
articles.summary: Loyd suffered a lower-body injury during Sunday's Game 1 loss.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces guard Jewell Loyd has been downgraded to out for Wednesday's playoff game against the Golden State Valkyries. She had been listed as doubtful.

Loyd is dealing with a left leg injury sustained in the third quarter of the Game 1 loss on Sunday. She couldn't return to the game.

Head coach Becky Hammon spoke to the media Tuesday and said they didn't yet have a report on Loyd. "We're trying to ramp them up, but now we've got to see how they feel and recover off of this little workout." A few hours later, the guard was listed as doubtful due to the injury.

On Wednesday, Hammon said Loyd was "likely" to be out for the contest. Hours later, the guard was downgraded to out.

Loyd isn't one of Las Vegas' star players, but if she is sidelined for the game, it will still hurt the Aces. The guard averages 8 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game.

Loyd averaged 25.9 minutes per game, though, and Las Vegas is already short on backcourt depth.

Before the injury Sunday, Loyd hadn't made either of her two shots from beyond the arc. She did play 17 minutes and added two rebounds and an assist.

Aces guard Dana Evans was listed as questionable and has been upgraded to probable. Forward Steph Talbot is considered questionable. Evans is dealing with a right knee issue, while Talbot is dealing with a lower left leg injury similar to Loyd's. Hammon said Wednesday both players will be game-time decisions.

With Loyd sidelined on Sunday night, guard Mai Yamamoto saw more playing time. She played 19 minutes, above her 15.1 average. Yamamoto finished the loss with just two points and an assist.

Las Vegas is down 1-0 in the best-of-five series.

articles.title: Trail Blazers have 'set themselves up to fail' by firing Braiden Bell over teenage tweets, attorney says
articles.summary: Braiden Bell's attorney calls the Portland Trail Blazers' morals clause "immoral" for firing the announcer over social media posts he made at age 15.
articles.body: Firing a grown man over social media posts he wrote as a 15-year-old kid has put the Portland Trail Blazers in hot water. Newly hired play-by-play announcer Braiden Bell was ousted shortly after taking the job when a local news report surfaced crude posts from 2012 and 2013. While Bell has navigated the situation with grace and issued an immediate public apology for his teenage posts, getting back into the Blazers' good graces remains a steep battle. Now, Bell's attorney, Arnie Herz, is pushing back against the franchise's approach. Speaking with OutKick, Herz addressed the societal shift toward retroactively punishing individuals for online posts. MEDIA SINKS TO NEW LOW BY DIGGING UP TWEETS THAT GOT ANNOUNCER FIRED BY COWARDLY BLAZERS "What we've become as a society is very much a gotcha and a teardown mindset," Herz explained. "If everything came to light of your most insensitive comments, your worst behaviors, you wouldn't be able to sustain this zero tolerance." Herz added that if the organization strictly enforced such a policy across the board, "I don't think there would be a single player, single member in the front office, a single coach, or a single fan who would be able to participate." Herz pointed out the utter absurdity of holding anyone to such a standard. "The only possible person who could be the play-by-play announcer based on a zero-tolerance standard is Mother Teresa," Herz added. "But there's three problems with that. One, she's not alive. Two, she knew nothing about basketball. And three, I don't think she'd want the job. So, that's it. There's no Saints, except in New Orleans, in football, and obviously, that's just the name." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! While morals clauses are common in sports, Herz argued applying them to teenage posts stretches the rule past common sense. "I'm a big fan of a morals clause," Herz noted. "I totally understand a team that has someone on their personnel who does something egregious, like being charged with a felony, making horrific comments as a grown-up in the course of their employment. ... But having a morals clause that's so broad that it is going to ensnare comments made by a teenage boy in early teenage years, 15, is immoral." "A morals clause properly drafted serves a very valuable moral purpose," Herz added. "And a morals clause overly broad becomes itself immoral. I think that's what we have here." Herz argued Portland's unyielding stance clashes directly with its own past. "Not only do they have no precedence, there's very few organizations in the world of sports that have shown greater leniency to giving second, third, fourth, and fifth chances than the Blazer organization," Herz stated. "This is an organization that's had significant issues in the past and have members on their staff on the court and off the court who have done far, far, far worse than what Mr. Bell did." He added that on-court value changes the rules entirely. NEW YORK TIMES LOSES DEFAMATION SUIT, ORDERED TO PAY $9.25M TO FORMER ALABAMA BASKETBALL PLAYER "When you're a big star, you make a lot of money, the team very much depends on you, the league depends on you, you get more slack," Herz admitted. "That's just the reality. If Braiden could hit a three and defend players like the starting five, we wouldn't be here right now." Herz warned that the franchise's stance sets a troublesome precedent for future hires. "If I'm legal counsel for the Blazers, I'm saying to the Blazers: 'You have to reinstate this guy. If you're gonna fire him for this, every single person on social media is gonna be scrutinizing every hire you make, every player you have on your roster, and it's going to consume you,'" Herz advised. "You've set yourself up to fail. Back off." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Herz urged both sides to acknowledge their mistakes and resolve the matter constructively. "Just like Braiden made a mistake, the Blazers made a mistake," Herz concluded. "Take responsibility, take accountability, let's move forward. Our goal is really to use this as a learning experience for everyone so that everyone could win." Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

articles.title: Dana Altman ends nearly four decade coaching career at Oregon: 'Stepping away is truly painful'
articles.summary: Dana Altman retires as Oregon Ducks basketball head coach after 16 seasons, with assistant Tony Stubblefield named interim for the upcoming campaign.
articles.body: The coach who has manned the sideline for more Oregon men’s basketball games than any other coach is going off into the sunset. Dana Altman has decided to retire after 16 seasons with the Ducks and nearly four decades as a Division I coach, the school announced Wednesday. Altman, 68, first took over Oregon’s program in 2010. Assistant coach Tony Stubblefield will assume Altman’s responsibilities on an interim basis beginning next season. "I've loved every minute of coaching here, and stepping away is difficult and truly painful," Altman said in a statement. "I love coaching, it's what I know best and what I've been fortunate enough to do for almost five decades. "... It's been the honor of my life to coach the Ducks," he added. Oregon football coach Dan Lanning was among those offering praise for Altman. "A great mentor, sees the game, and obviously a Hall of Fame coach with what he’s been able to accomplish," Lanning said. "I love his story, and how grounded he is, and he’s as good as they come." BASKETBALL HALL OF FAMER DON NELSON DEAD AT 86 Altman’s announcement came as a surprise, but the Ducks have experienced some upheaval. They struggled last season, going 12-20, and the program lost nine players to the transfer portal and three to graduation in the offseason. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Stubblefield has spent two stints as an assistant to Altman at Oregon. He left to become head coach at DePaul from 2021-24 before returning to the Ducks. "Winning 382 games over 16 years, including making nine NCAA Tournaments and a Final Four, is an incredible track record. But the record book tells only part of the story," Oregon athletic director Rob Mullins said. TODD GOLDEN WILL COACH THE FLORIDA GATORS NEXT SEASON ... OR WILL HE? "Dana and Reva have given so much of themselves to this university and to the young men who played for him, and we thank him for all his contributions to Oregon student-athletes, the game of basketball, and the University of Oregon." The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Fans are wondering if Florida Panthers are cursed as another star exits game Wednesday night
articles.summary: Aleksander Barkov's latest injury and Brad Marchand's scary exit have Florida Panthers fans wondering if the team is cursed after back-to-back Cups.
articles.body: A little less than 16 months ago, the question surrounding the National Hockey League was whether or not the Florida Panthers were on the fast track to becoming the sport's next dynasty. They had just vanquished the Edmonton Oilers for the second year in a row to capture back-to-back Stanley Cups, and many fans were wondering if they had a chance to become the first team to three-peat since the New York Islanders won four straight from 1980-83. Then the injuries started to pile up, beginning right as the Cup celebration ended with star winger Matthew Tkachuk needing adductor surgery. OTTAWA SENATORS OWNER CLAIMS KEITH TKACHUK AND MATTHEW TKACHUK SWAYED BRADY'S TRADE REQUEST Tkachuk would be out for the first half of the season, but his injury was only the tip of the iceberg. The Panthers famously lost captain Aleksander Barkov for the year thanks to a torn ACL, and other key contributors like sniper Sam Reinhart, defender Seth Jones, and two-way wizard Anton Lundell also missed multiple weeks in the season with a bevy of injuries. 2026 was supposed to be the bounceback year for the Cats, as Barkov and the rest of his merry band of champions were thought to be fully healthy. Then, just two games into the season, the Panthers captain went down awkwardly in an eerily similar fashion to his ACL injury a little more than a year earlier, causing Florida fans to wince. Barkov was given a supremely positive diagnosis relative to what the news could have been — a 6-8 week recovery period — but before Panthers fans could even finish their sighs of relief, another integral piece to their 2025 Cup run went down in a heap. When it rains it pours, and Florida losing Brad Marchand for any stretch of time is less than ideal. The 38-year-old forward defied Father Time during the 2025 Stanley Cup Playoffs, scoring 10 goals and 10 assists in 23 postseason games, but this latest injury could be one that keeps him out for a while. Marchand was already recovering from an injury at the end of last season, and the fears are this could be serious given the fact he was unable to put any weight on his leg as he was helped off the ice Wednesday night (the most likely outcome seems to be an MCL injury). THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! This rash of injuries over the past year plus has fans wondering whether the Panthers sold their souls for those back-to-back Cups. Fellow OutKick writer and hockey fanatic Matt Reigle even asked me if there were any electrical substations located near Amarant Bank Arena. While I'm not sure about that, I have opined for quite some time now that the Cats may be cursed, and the Marchy injury isn't exactly helping to assuage those concerns. If you're a Panthers fan looking for a positive, then consider the fact that the Barkov injury wasn't as bad as initially feared, and there is a world where Marchand gets a similar diagnosis. The Cats also went out and acquired Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk to help bolster the depth on the roster as well, so if anyone can withstand the injury bug early in the season, it's Florida. Also, we are only four games into the year, but the Panthers are leading the division even without their captain and their playoff ace. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The sky may not be falling in Sunrise, FL, but there is still plenty of reason to have one foot inside the doomsday bunker for the time being.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton buys student section tickets for Iowa State students in his preseason return
articles.summary: In his return to his alma mater, Tyrese Haliburton bought out the student section tickets for all Iowa State students for the Pacers first preseason game in...
articles.body:
AMES, Iowa — Iowa State students got in free to Tyrese Haliburton's homecoming game Wednesday night, thanks to the superstar himself.

Sixteen months after tearing his Achilles in the 2025 NBA Finals, Haliburton is making his return to NBA action at Hilton Coliseum, his alma mater, for Indiana's first preseason game against the Minnesota Timberwolves .

In his return, he wanted to cultivate the college basketball fan environment. So, he paid for every single student section ticket himself.

"I know that nobody is as passionate about Iowa State as the current students, so I'm excited for them to be there and just experience all that," Haliburton said at practice on Wednesday. "The college basketball environment is much better than the NBA, from a top to bottom perspective, so I'm excited for there to be a college basketball vibe in there."

Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton visits Peyton Manning Children's Hospital

The student section at Hilton Coliseum sits behind both baskets, and the line to get a spot wrapped around the building by the time doors opened an hour and half before game time. Inside, every student got a yellow 'Cyclone Hali' t-shirt, which depicted Haliburton wrapped up in a cyclone.

Haliburton didn't know how many tickets he bought, Pacers head coach Carlisle said, but he estimated it was in the thousands.

"This is just another one of those amazing gestures of Tyrese's family," Carlisle said. "We pulled in here, and it took a while to get in here, there's a huge line at the front door, and it looks like a bunch of students. I've been in here for games a couple times, and this is one of the best venue in all of college basketball, and so I'm expecting it's going to be pretty cool here tonight."

Haliburton knows, too, that not all the students will be rooting for him — especially because the majority of Iowans in this area are Timberwolves fans. There were some students in Timberwolves jerseys in line, and even someone in a Milwaukee Bucks jersey waiting to get in.

The student section at Hilton Coliseum spans behind both baskets, and the line was wrapped around the building by the time students were let in.

"I don't know if it'll be all Pacers fans in there, it'll be some Timberwolves fans too," Haliburton said on Wednesday with a laugh. "But it'll be fun, I'm excited for everybody to experience Hilton Coliseum."

articles.title: Atlanta Dream to call State Farm Arena home in 2027 amid WNBA boom
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream will have a new home with 17,000 seats in 2027. State Farm Arena is now the WNBA team's base.
articles.body:
ATLANTA ― The Atlanta Dream are getting new digs for the 2027 WNBA season.

On Tuesday, the organization announced it will call State Farm Arena home next year. The move comes as part of a multi-year agreement with the facility to host home games and amid record growth for the league. Next season, the WNBA will move to 50 games and State Farm will host the Dream's 25 home contests.

The Dream sold out every game during the last three seasons at its current home, Gateway Center Arena, a space which holds 3,500-plus seats. Within that same span, Atlanta played multiple games at State Farm, including six regular-season and two playoff games this season, with another postseason game tipping off Wednesday against the New York Liberty . The venue was sold out eight times and had multiple games at full capacity, with more than 17,000 seats.

"We didn't have playoff games (at State Farm Arena) last year ... but we had a couple of games there, and they felt like playoff games. So I think for us to have had those during the season and have the outcome that we had, I think it helps us get ready for this environment," Dream guard Rhyne Howard said.

"Our fans are gonna show up every day, whether we're here (at Gateway Center Area or) whether we're in State Farm, but I think being able to have all of our games there ― it gives us more. Obviously, there's more people, but I think you give more people the opportunity to come cheer for you."

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

"Something (Dream co-owner) Suzanne Abair said to me ... she said, we don't believe in betting on women because when you place a bet, you expect that you might lose your money. But when you invest, you expect a return," Morgan Shaw Parker, the team president and chief operating officer, said on Wednesday. "You have to invest it. It takes a lot out of our leadership, takes a lot out of our ownership. It costs. The operating budget is extremely important, but how do you maintain that? You set the vision, and you don't take your foot off the gas."

Shaw Parker also said the addition of Angel Reese impacted the decision to move arenas.

"It was a huge impact to our organization with Angel coming. What I've always said is we would have never been able to attract someone like Angel Reese if we weren't ready to receive her," Shaw Parker said. "Atlanta is here for her. She is here for Atlanta, but what she's brought is undeniable."

Atlanta, which joined the league as an expansion franchise in 2008, began its WNBA tenure at Philips Arena (now renamed State Farm Arena) the same year and played at the venue through the 2016 season. It then spent two seasons at Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion from 2017-2018 before returning to State Farm in 2019. Following the 2019 season, the Dream moved to Gateway Center in 2020, where it has played seven seasons.

Shaw Parker confirmed the Dream are also exploring plans for a women's specific arena in Atlanta in the future.

Atlanta is currently competing in the 2026 WNBA playoffs as the No. 4 seed after finishing 30-14 for the second consecutive season. It swept the Washington Mystics, 2-0, in the first round and is currently in the semifinals for the first time since 2018. The Dream are up 1-0 over the Liberty as of this publication.

articles.title: Why Dodgers’ Dave Roberts still believes in Shohei Ohtani despite offensive struggles
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are tinkering with how they’re using Shohei Ohtani against the Atlanta Braves. Manager Dave Roberts made one stunning lineup change i...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are tinkering with how they're using Shohei Ohtani against the Atlanta Braves. Manager Dave Roberts made one stunning lineup change involving Ohtani before Game 4 of the MLB Playoffs. But it doesn't mean Roberts is wavering from his belief in Ohtani despite recent struggles.

Roberts addressed the lapses before heading out to Truist Park for warmups.

"It's not what we all expect, what he expects from himself," Roberts began. "But I do feel that just the talent, the care, it's going to happen."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Roberts dipped into the big key moving forward for Ohtani, and the Dodgers.

"So I think it's just up to all of us to keep winning baseball games, and then at some point he's going to come to life," Roberts added.

Dodger fans became spoiled with seeing Ohtani lead off at the bat. Los Angeles wanted to set the tone right away with its top power hitter. Especially with his 35 lead off homers attached to him during his career.

But Roberts and LA made the decision to place him down to fifth in the order for the Tuesday contest. Roberts now has slightly moved up Ohtani, but plugging him at fourth in the order.

Some fans are wondering if Ohtani ever recovered from a previous MLB Injury that limited him toward the end of the regular season. Now LA and Roberts will aim to reignite him as a cleanup hitter.

Los Angeles enters Game 4 of the National League Divisional Series (NLDS) with a 2-1 series lead.

articles.title: Buss siblings file formal opposition after Jeanie Buss' attempts to block remaining sale of Lakers stake
articles.summary: The Buss family legal battle over their remaining stake in the Lakers appears to be far from over.
articles.body:
The Buss family legal battle over the Los Angeles Lakers continued on Wednesday.

The five Buss siblings who voted to sell the rest of the family trust's shares in the franchise — Jim, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jessie — filed a formal opposition in court on Wednesday after unresolved settlement discussions with their other sister, Jeanie Buss, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

Jeanie had previously filed a petition in Los Angeles Superior Court to attempt to block the five siblings from selling the family's remaining 17.8% stake in the Lakers, which she claimed was a scheme to remove her from her role as the team's governor.

"Jimmy, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss, the five of six siblings who voted to sell the Trust's shares in the Lakers, today filed their formal opposition, demonstrating that Jeanie Buss's petition is legally and factually baseless," the five siblings said in a statement. "While discussions among the siblings continue, their focus remains on facilitating the proposed transaction and the Trust's participation in it, while ensuring that all beneficiaries, including Jeanie, are treated equally. "Today's filing is a necessary step to protect those interests and ensure the transaction proceeds on schedule."

"Jimmy, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss, the five of six siblings who voted to sell the Trust's shares in the Lakers, today filed their formal opposition, demonstrating that Jeanie Buss's petition is legally and factually baseless," the five siblings said in a statement. "While discussions among the siblings continue, their focus remains on facilitating the proposed transaction and the Trust's participation in it, while ensuring that all beneficiaries, including Jeanie, are treated equally.

"Today's filing is a necessary step to protect those interests and ensure the transaction proceeds on schedule."

Mark Walter, who purchased a majority of the Buss family's share of the Lakers last year, announced earlier this fall that he was selling his stake in the team to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger at a record $12.5 billion valuation. The five siblings then reportedly voted to invoke a "tag-along" clause to sell their remaining stake in the team to Kushner and Iger.

Jeanie, however, does not want to sell and called any vote to sell the team "void." She filed a 97-page petition that included five causes of action , and argued that selling the team doesn't make any financial sense. She also asked the court to instruct her co-trustees to observe a 2017 court order that requires they "take all actions reasonably available to ensure Jeanie's appointment as Controlling Owner" of the Lakers.

NBA rules require that a team governor own at least 15% of a team. Jeanie was going to remain in her role as governor for the next four years under Kushner and Iger, though that can't happen if her siblings prevail and they sell the rest of their shares.

This is just the latest feud among the Buss siblings since their father, Jerry Buss, died in 2013. The biggest issue was back in 2017, when Jeanie fired Jim as the Lakers' head of basketball operations, which led to Johnny challenging her control of the team. Jerry left her control of the team as part of the trust, and she ended up winning a court decision that said her siblings were obligated to ensure she remains the team's controlling owner.

It's unclear if that order still applies, as the Buss family is not the controlling owner of the team anymore. Jeanie simply wants to keep control of the team's minority ownership of the team.

The move to sell the team by the siblings makes sense, especially since Jerry put a "last man standing" provision in his trust. That would transfer ownership of the team and funds to the remaining siblings when one of the six of them dies, rather than to their own families. But if the siblings sell before their own deaths, they can pass money along to their respective families and children.

Clearly, things within the Buss family haven't settled down any. With a formal opposition now filed, the family is headed toward another, likely messy, court battle.

articles.summary: The WNBA semifinals continue with Game 2 on Wednesday.
articles.body: After the Dream put together a dominant defensive performance in Game 1, they'll surely look to replicate that in Game 2 against the Liberty on Wednesday night. But Atlanta will again be without Allisha Gray, who injured her hand in the first half of Sunday's game. Will New York be more prepared for the Dream attack that created 19 turnovers (14 steals) en route to a 10-point win? Can veteran DeWanna Bonner have another monster game (23 points, 9 rebounds off the bench) to help supplement the offense with Gray out?
